paragraphs: Baker, here's the big idea. The LORD does what He says, and He does it on time. He told Pharaoh a final plague was coming, and at midnight it came (Exodus 12:29). Israel's stay in Egypt lasted 430 years, and the LORD brought them out "to the very day" (Exodus 12:40-41), so I think that should make every one of us breathe easier about the things we're still waiting on.

Now look at who is leading this exodus. Pharaoh, the man who kept saying no, is the one saying "Get up, leave my people" (Exodus 12:31). The Egyptians hurry Israel out the door, and the LORD gave the people "favor in the sight of the Egyptians" (Exodus 12:36). No army, no battle plan, no grand speech from Israel. The LORD brought them out (Exodus 12:51), and that's the whole story of how they got free.

And friend, the Passover rules say something too. The foreigner who lives among them can join in (Exodus 12:48), and "The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you." (Exodus 12:49). The people did just as the LORD commanded (Exodus 12:50), and the night became a vigil to remember for generations (Exodus 12:42). So here's what to carry out of this one: the LORD frees His people, He makes room at His table for others, and He asks us to remember what He did. This road is only getting started, and I'm already excited.
